report.summary: Chunk 2 of daedalus/council/publish.py: defines helper functions (_bus_path, _turns_of, _chain_head, _quorum_counts, _evidence_paths) and the main render_markdown function. 37 claims checked: 0 broken, 4 uncheckable, rest kept.
risks: _bus_path | high | Fallback to `DEFAULT_BUS_DIR/{council_id}.jsonl` may produce path outside working directory if DEFAULT_BUS_DIR is absolute or contains '..'. | Check DEFAULT_BUS_DIR definition in this file or module.

_quorum_counts | medium | When both vendor lists and integer counts are present, the function prefers list length over integer. This could mask a mismatch between list and integer. | Verify that the integer fields are always consistent with list lengths in practice.

_chain_head | medium | Fallback to last turn's entry_sha assumes the transcript is an append-only chain; if transcript is mutated out of order, head may be incorrect. | Confirm that transcript construction guarantees append-only order.

render_markdown | low | The advisory field is checked with `advisory is not True`; if advisory is an integer 1 or a truthy object, the warning block is skipped. | Confirm that advisory is always a boolean True/False in practice.

render_markdown | low | The dissents section uses `isinstance(item, (str, bytes))` to detect plain strings; if a vendor object is a string subclass, it may be misattributed. | Unlikely but possible; check for string subclass usage.

handoff.purpose: Define helper functions for bus path, turn extraction, chain head, quorum counts, evidence paths; implement render_markdown function to produce markdown string from verdict and transcript.

symbols.name: _bus_path
symbols.note: Private helper to determine canonical bus path from verdict/transcript fields, falling back to DEFAULT_BUS_DIR/{council_id}.jsonl.

symbols.name: _turns_of
symbols.note: Extracts turn list from transcript, which may be a list, tuple, Mapping, or other object with turns/records/entries fields.

symbols.name: _chain_head
symbols.note: Returns chain head digest from transcript or verdict fields, falling back to last turn's entry_sha.

symbols.name: _quorum_counts
symbols.note: Returns (answered, requested, answered_vendors, missing_vendors) tuple, preferring vendor lists over integer counts.

symbols.name: _evidence_paths
symbols.note: Extracts evidence path strings from verdict evidence and paths fields.

symbols.name: render_markdown
symbols.note: Main public function: renders verdict and transcript as markdown string. Pure function with no I/O.

claims.text: Where the canonical record lives. Explicit field wins; otherwise derived from the council id, which is how ``bus.py`` names the file.
claims.why: Code checks explicit fields first, then falls back to council_id-based path.

claims.text: A transcript may be the turn list itself, or an object/dict carrying one.
claims.why: Code handles None, Mapping, list/tuple, and other objects with fields.

claims.text: The chain head digest a reader verifies the bus against. Explicit field wins; otherwise the last turn's entry_sha, which IS the head by construction in an append-only chain.
claims.why: Code checks transcript fields, then verdict fields, then last turn's entry_sha.

claims.text: (answered, requested, answered_vendors, missing_vendors). Counts are derived from the vendor LISTS when present, because a list is checkable against the transcript and a bare integer is not.
claims.why: Code uses list lengths when available, falls back to integer fields.

claims.text: Paths named by the evidence, for the path-marker half of the floor.
claims.why: Code extracts paths from evidence items and paths field.

claims.text: Render one council deliberation as markdown.

Order is deliberate and load-bearing: outcome and the quorum honesty line lead, so a degraded council is the first thing a reader sees and cannot be skimmed past. Then EVERY dissent verbatim with its author -- BEFORE the convergence, because the dissent is the only part that could not have come from asking one model twice. Then where the vendors converged, evidence digests, per-vendor cost/latency, the deliberation itself, and finally the provenance footer (bus path + chain head) that lets a reader verify all of it offline.
claims.why: Code follows this order: outcome, quorum, dissents, convergence, evidence, cost/latency, deliberation, footer.

claims.text: Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.
claims.why: Function only constructs strings; no I/O, network, or gate calls in this chunk.

claims.text: CONVERGENCE, not "majority". A majority is a DECISION; convergence is an OBSERVATION about what the vendors said. The council package carries no approve/reject/score/majority/consensus field on purpose -- absence of the field is the control, not a docstring -- and a rendering that reintroduces the word structurally reintroduces the temptation to read it as a verdict. The legacy aliases are kept only so an older payload still renders.
claims.why: Code uses convergence field with aliases including 'majority', but renders as 'convergence' in heading.

claims.text: The advisory banner is UNCONDITIONAL. A verdict arriving without the marker is a contract violation, so we say so instead of quietly rendering it as if it carried authority.
claims.why: Code always adds 'ADVISORY ONLY' line, and checks advisory field for warning.

claims.text: Quorum honesty, at the top. A short council is a weaker signal and that must be impossible to miss -- it is a warning block, not a footnote.
claims.why: Quorum section is rendered early with warning if degraded.

claims.text: DISSENT LEADS. Not a stylistic choice: the dissent is the only content in this document that could not have been produced by asking one model twice. Convergence among vendors with overlapping training data is cheap; the objection is what four egress paths were actually paid for. Rendering it after -- and therefore below -- the agreement makes the informative half read as a footnote to the uninformative half.
claims.why: Dissents section appears before convergence section.

claims.text: A vendor that did not speak has no content; an empty fence is noise that makes a silent turn look like an empty answer.
claims.why: Code only adds verbatim block if text is non-empty.

claims.text: Evidence digests: what was actually deliberated over, by hash.
claims.why: Section renders evidence items with label and sha256.

claims.text: Per-vendor cost and latency: what the opinion cost, per independent voice.
claims.why: Section renders table with vendor, model, cost, latency.

claims.text: The deliberation itself -- this comment IS the rendering of the bus.

bus.py records "refused" / "unavailable" / "budget_exhausted" / "anomaly" rather than dropping the vendor, so rendering the status is the difference between "three vendors agreed" and "one was never asked".
claims.why: Reference to bus.py behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send are NAMED, not counted -- a vendor reasoning over less evidence than the others is not an equal voice, and hiding that would make the roster look stronger than it was.
claims.why: Code renders withheld paths list with note.

claims.text: Provenance footer: how to check this rendering against the record.
claims.why: Footer section renders bus path and chain head.

observations.what: _bus_path uses DEFAULT_BUS_DIR without checking if it is defined; assumes it exists as a global constant.
_quorum_counts may return requested=0 if both integer and list fields are missing, then sets requested=answered, which could hide a missing roster.
render_markdown uses _field with many aliases; if multiple aliases exist, the first one found wins, which may produce unexpected output if order is not as expected.
The advisory warning block uses `advisory is not True`; if advisory is 1 (integer), it will not trigger the warning. The comment says 'unconditional' but the check is conditional.

In dissents section, if item is a string/bytes, it is treated as unattributed with no model; but the code later attempts to extract author/text/model from non-string items, which may fail if item is not a mapping.
